0.content: Yoimiya's father and the previous owner of Naganohara Fireworks. Since an accident his hearing has been poor, so customers must repeat themselves, and he cheerfully answers questions nobody asked. He launches into long tales of how people first learned that ground minerals burn in colours. As a child Yoimiya took his constant smile as agreement with everything she said; when she learned the truth she kept talking anyway, because it makes him happy and keeps him from being lonely. He found her discarded Vision in the storeroom and taught her its worth. Her favourite of his stories: a firework's last sparks become rain and snow, nourish the land, and one day rise into the sky again.

1.comment: Yoimiya: Naganohara Fireworks and the formula slips
1.content: The Naganohara family shop in Hanamizaka, Inazuma City, and the namesake of the Naganohara Fireworks Show. It began over a century ago when the Yashiro Commission ordered a commemorative display, and has since become a festival where everyone lights their own fireworks before the owner's grand finale. Every customer who orders a commemorative firework receives a note readable only by the family. It records the formula, so whether ten or a hundred years pass, the Naganohara can make exactly the same firework again. Yoimiya calls the family "keepers of the gate" to past memories. The shop also sells toys and knickknacks. Its customers are mostly regulars, and the family works "so that we won't let everyone down".

2.content: The Yashiro Commission and its shrine maidens run Inazuma's festivals, and Yoimiya creates their spectacle, so the two have worked together for years. Ayaka asked for the Shogun's emblem in Yoimiya's first show and got it cleverly hidden in the display. Yoimiya says Ayaka always lets her finish and answers seriously, unlike people in the other Commissions; "ladylike" was made for her. After a late-night festival meeting Yoimiya suggested a public bath, and Ayaka went red, since noble ladies cannot use them. Ayaka defends fireworks against public-order objections. In 2.0 she sent the Traveler to Yoimiya to free Master Masakatsu.

3.comment: Yoimiya: The Vision Hunt Decree and Master Masakatsu
3.content: Under the Vision Hunt Decree, Hanamizaka craftsman Master Masakatsu made counterfeit Visions for the resistance, and Yoimiya kept her own Vision thanks to them. When the Traveler first arrived at Naganohara Fireworks, Tenryou samurai were confiscating a man's Vision. Yoimiya pulled the Traveler aside; the samurai left with a fake she had swapped in. Masakatsu had since been arrested. Yoimiya had been thinking of breaking him out but did not want to embarrass Ayaka, so she joined the Traveler. She led them in by a way she had scouted beforehand and set off a firework "gift" to draw the guards while they freed the tortured craftsman; Kujou Sara let them go for the sake of his health.

4.content: To Hanamizaka's children Yoimiya is a heroic big sister who always has a solution. She plays timeless games with them and hunts shiny trinkets with them. She protects their fantasies: she told them the Great Mujina Youkai is cute, mischievous and harmless, and gave them firework "weapons" to scare it off. She refused to debunk a tale whose real reasons she did not know. An old folksong about rainbows turning into wish-fireworks led the children to bring her "shiny" treasures. She makes each child a firework of their own for creek pebbles or shell shards, and takes them to return anything expensive to its owner. She wants them to have a happy time even during the lockdown.

5.content: Itto is as popular with the children as she is, and every play session turns into a showdown: a bowl of ramen soup in one go, sour plums without a grimace, with the children cheering and betting. She "can't let him beat me". She was surprised to learn his gang was real and he was not just idle. He buys her custom knickknacks to challenge his "nemesis" Kujou Sara. He grumbles that her fireworks and toys steal his thunder, and insists anyone shorter than him is a kid who should side with him.
